Article Title: ‘Jhooth ki goonj’ site ‘fact-checks’ Rahul’s student meet claims
Article Text:
“Here are all the lies Rahul Gandhi told during his so-called Chhatron Ki Goonj,” the site reads.

NEW DELHI: With Rahul Gandhi looking to ride on the impact of his ‘Chhatron ki goonj’ initiative in his campaign against govt, a website, ‘jhooth ki goonj’, claiming to fact-check his assertions at the four editions of the event so far, has been grabbing attention in saffron circles.The digital counterpunch against Rahul’s campaign obviously complements BJP ’s efforts, but the party has denied any association with the website. The website itself makes no direct mention of the people behind it, but as it trended on social media, some attributed its creation to “nationalist researchers” and Gen Z-ers, the very generation Rahul is targeting in his hops across cities.“Here are all the lies Rahul Gandhi told during his so-called Chhatron Ki Goonj,” the site reads, making no secret of where it stands in his pitch against BJP. It says Rahul has made 40 claims in his four interactions, and all of them were either false or misleading (29 false and 11 misleading).It adds that Rahul had said that out of 1,000 youths looking for jobs, about 36 will get permanent jobs. Roughly, 300 will remain unemployed and about 700 will become gig workers, he said. Rejecting the claim as false, the website cites PLFS unit-level data to claim that 26 out of every 100 graduates aged 15-29 in 2025 have salaried jobs.Taking on another claim that Rahul had made — about 29% women faced physical violence — the website says he relied on old NFHS data. “Since the Modi govt came to office, the NFHS data shows a clear decline in spousal physical and/or sexual violence: from 37.2% in (2005-06) to 22.3% in (2023-24),” it says.How much impact the website will make is anyone’s guess, but it has certainly got pro-BJP voices on social media excited. “From tweaked numbers to fabricated stats, every single claim has now been fact-checked,” one user said.
Article Summary: “Here are all the lies Rahul Gandhi told during his so-called Chhatron Ki Goonj,” the site reads. It says Rahul has made 40 claims in his four interactions, and all of them were either false or misleading (29 false and 11 misleading)

Article Title: Garg Aviation’s trainer aircraft crashes in Kanpur, 2 killed
Article Text:
An official examines the wreckage of a Tecnam aircraft following a fatal crash in Kanpur.

NEW DELHI: A training aircraft belonging to Kanpur’s Garg Aviation crashed on Thursday, killing two — an instructor and a trainee pilot — on board. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation said in a statement the Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft (VT-NBV) crashed about five nautical miles from Kanpur Civil Airport, near Ganga Barrage.“The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of Kanpur Civil Airport. There were two persons on board, a trainee pilot and an instructor. Both sustained fatal injuries in the accident. A team of three officials from the DGCA is proceeding to the site for necessary regulatory oversight and coordination,” said the DGCA statement.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules. The circumstances and cause of the accident will be determined through the investigation,” it added.Senior pilots call for a thorough investigation into the flying school operations.On June 26, 2026, a trainee pilot had got grievously injured while deboarding VT-NBV with the propeller running at Kanpur’s Chakeri Airport. Following this lapse, the DGCA had on June 28 said in a statement that it had “directed VT-NBV aircraft should not be utilised pending the probe.” Subsequently the aircraft started flying again till it crashed on Thursday.
Article Summary: The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of Kanpur Civil Airport. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules”

Article Title: Ex-IAF vice-chief Kapoor says India’s 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s, country must partner with global consortiums like FCAS or GCAP for 6th-gen programme
Article Text:
Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force. “Why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other” he said.

Sriram Kartik sweeps 10 awards including the ‘Best Junior contestant’ across Carnatic vocal and mrudangam; prizes presented by eminent Vidwan Sikkil Gurucharan on 23 Aug 2026 in MumbaiA fifteen-year-old from Powai has won ten awards at the Music Competition 2026 conducted by Sri Shanmukhananda Bharatiya Sangeetha Vidyalaya and Natya Vidyalaya, competing in both Carnatic vocal and mrudangam.Sriram Kartik, a Class X IGCSE student at Podar International School, received the awards at the prize distribution ceremony held on Sunday (Aug 23, 2026) on the occasion of Shanmukhananda's Carnataka Sangeetha Pon Mazhai Thiruvizha, at the Sri Shanmukhananda Fine Arts and Sangeetha Sabha in Matunga. The prizes were presented by Shanmukha Sangeetha Shiromani Vidwan Shri Sikkil Gurucharan, the eminent Carnatic vocalist, who presided over the ceremony.Vidwan Sikkil C Gurucharan is a leading Indian Carnatic classical vocalist and youth ambassador for the art form. A singer born into a family of flautists, and grandson of Sikkil Kunjumani, the elder of the Sikkil Sisters, he trained under B Krishnamurthy and Vaigal S. Gnanaskandan, himself a disciple of Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and gave his first concert at The Music Academy, Chennai at the age of twelve. Recipient of the Kalaimamani award from the Tamil Nadu government in 2020, Sikkil C Gurucharan has been featured by India Today as one of the 35 Game Changers Under 35 in India.Sriram Kartik won 9 individual prizes — five first prizes, three seconds and one third. He was also awarded a cash prize for being the Best Junior contestant winning the maximum number of prizes in the 10-to-15 years age category.The competition, the Vidyalaya's 70th annual, was held on February 7 and 8 across Carnatic vocal, violin, veena, mrudangam, Hindustani vocal, sitar and tabla. It drew more than 300 participants from across India and overseas, contesting in three age groups: 10 to 15, 16 to 28, and 29 and above.Sriram's two mrudangam prizes came in the only two categories open to his age group — a first for tani avartanam in roopakam and misra chapu talams, and a second for adi talam with five jathi mohras, awarded under the TS Nandakumar's Percussive Arts Centre Endowment and the Guru TS Nandakumar Endowment respectively.His seven vocal prizes spanned first places in compositions of the Trinity, varnams, Purandaradasa kritis; the Silver Lamp Prize for keertanams and kritis; second places in Subramania Bharatiyar compositions and Tamizh compositions; and a third in GNB kritis.Every prize at Shanmukhananda is attached to an endowment instituted in the name of an artist, a patron or an institution. He won awards under the following endowments namely - GNB Endowment, the Kalki Memorial, the Dr S Pinakapani Endowment, the BVS Iyengar Memorial and the Lakshmi Gopalakrishna Memorial. The Best Junior award came under the Smt. Parvathy Subramaniam Endowment and S Ramakrishnan Memorial.Sriram began learning the mrudangam at the age of five, under Acharya Ratna Vidwan Mumbai Shri Shankaranarayanan at Powai Fine Arts. A decade on, he has kept at it through the school years in which most students of classical music quietly stop — the age at which coaching classes, board examinations and the ordinary pull of everything else tend to close the practice room door for good.Sustaining it alongside school is the part a prize list does not show. Practice sessions run two and a half to three hours. Nine vocal categories at 5-6 compositions a piece meant something close to 45-50 pieces in which he participated of which he won prizes across seven categories, readied to a standard that would survive a judging panel, with two percussion categories besides.He now receives higher tutelage in mrudangam from Padma Vibhushan and Sangeet Natak Academi Awardee Vidwan Dr Umayalpuram K Sivaraman, and trains in Carnatic vocal music under Acharya Ratnakara Vidwan Sherthalai Dr KN Renganatha Sharma and Vidushi Dr Mohana Sharma. He holds a CCRT Scholarship for Mrudangam from the ministry of culture, and presented his mrudangam arangetram in June last year, the day after his fourteenth birthday.
Article Summary: Sriram Kartik, a Class X IGCSE student at Podar International School, received the awards at the prize distribution ceremony held on Sunday (Aug 23, 2026) The competition, the Vidyalaya's 70th annual, was held on February 7 and 8 across Carnatic vocal, violin, veena, mrudangam, Hindustani vocal, sitar and tabla.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami joins Tapkeshwar Mahadev Shobha Yatra
Article Text:
Uttarakhand CM Dhami joins Tapkeshwar Mahadev Shobha Yatra

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Wednesday participated in the Shobha Yatra of Tapkeshwar Mahadev Ji, which commenced from Shivaji Dharamshala in Arhat Bazaar and will pass through major routes of Dehradun before reaching the Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple.Speaking on the occasion, Dhami extended his greetings to devotees and saints associated with the annual procession and highlighted the religious significance of the event, held during the holy month of Shravan.Speaking to reporters, he said, "First of all, I extend my heartiest congratulations and best wishes to all the devotees and the revered saints who organize the grand annual Tapkeshwar Mahadev procession, an event that draws a massive sea of worshippers. Taking place during the holy month of Shravan, this event involves worship, the abhishek of Lord Bholenath, and the grand procession. The Char Dham Yatra is currently underway, and its second phase is set to begin in September; while the monsoon season often brings challenges regarding roads and travel, we are now fully prepared for this next phase. We are also making comprehensive preparations for the 2027 Kumbh Mela in Haridwar, ensuring that all arrangements are in place for the devotees."The Chief Minister also spoke about the state government's preparations for the return of Agniveers and the establishment of a dedicated Agniveer Cell in Uttarakhand.On the Agniveer Cell, Dhami said the initiative aims to provide employment opportunities to Agniveers returning after completing their service, while making use of the training and skills they acquire during their tenure in the armed forces."Across the entire nation, one out of every five soldiers serving the country hails from Uttarakhand. Every family here shares a bond with the armed forces, a bond that spans generations, not just the present day. I, too, am the son of a soldier and am fulfilling my responsibilities with that perspective. The objective behind establishing the Agniveer Cell is to ensure that all Agniveers returning from service find employment opportunities here in some capacity. We want their service to continue, and thanks to the excellent training and education they receive, they will be fit in every respect and capable of entering any field. We are preparing for the arrival of the first batch, and the Cabinet has already approved the dedicated Agniveer Cell. We are actively working on this; 'Devbhoomi' has a high concentration of soldiers, and our soldiers, along with their families, are among our top priorities," CM said.The Shobha Yatra will culminate at the revered Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple, with devotees participating in the annual religious procession.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami participated in the Shobha Yatra of Tapkeshwar Mahadev Ji. The event involves worship, the abhishek of Lord Bholenath, and the grand procession. One out of every five soldiers serving the country hails from Uttarakhand.

NEW DELHI: BJP on Wednesday attacked leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi , over his recent “smash the patriarchy” remark, accusing him of hypocrisy and questioning whether he applies the same principle within his own Congress party Addressing a press conference, BJP leader and MP Bansuri Swaraj referred to Congress leader’s August 22 remarks at an event in Pune, where he spoke about challenging patriarchal attitudes and restrictions placed on women.“On August 22, Leader of Opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi tried to create a new false narrative in this country. He says, ‘Smash the patriarchy.’ I am all for it,” Swaraj said.“But I want to ask Rahul Gandhi ji, do you limit the slogan of ‘smash the patriarchy’ only to the stage in Pune? Do you practise political patriarchy within your own Congress party?” she added.Swaraj accused Rae Bareli MP of lacking a “vision” and “positive agenda”, alleging that he uses material prepared by his research team to mislead voters and young people.Swaraj said the Congress should begin by examining its own record if it wants to challenge patriarchy.She cited the controversy involving Congress leader Supriya Shrinate's social media account after BJP MP Kangana Ranaut was given the party ticket from Mandi during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.Swaraj described the remarks posted from the account as “extremely objectionable”.She also referred to comments made by Congress leader Randeep Surjewala about BJP leader and actor Hema Malini at a rally in Kaithal in April 2024.Swaraj said Surjewala was subsequently barred from campaigning for 48 hours following action over the remarks.“But Rahul Gandhi did not ‘smash the patriarchy’ then either. There was no such statement from him. Instead, he once again chose to remain silent,” she said.Swaraj also criticised Rahul over what she described as a “highly objectionable joke” involving Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni of Italy, saying Gandhi had participated in it along with Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit.“It does not befit the leader of opposition of the country to make such statements. It appears that leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi now makes statements solely for their meme and reel value,” Swaraj said.BJP MP further said, "I want to ask Rahul Gandhi, why is there not a single woman leader in Karnataka and Himachal? Why did he oppose the Women's Reservation Bill? And you are talking about women empowerment?"Highlighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's governance model centered on women-led development, Swaraj stated, "You constantly criticize Narendra Modi, but he is a leader committed to empowering women. Currently, 48 percent of India’s women are leading startups around the world. Rahul Gandhi, I am calling you out for your misogyny. This nation deserves a better Leader of the Opposition than you, Mr. Rahul Gandhi. "Congress MP's remarks came during the Congress' ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign in Pune, where he addressed thousands of women and girl students.He said the campaign was aimed at challenging a patriarchal system that, according to him, gives men greater freedom while imposing restrictions on women.Former Congress president referred to a video of PM Modi that he said was released after a protest at Jantar Mantar. He alleged that the Prime Minister was “culturally shocked” when girls protesting used cuss words but had no objection to boys using similar language.“Our fight is against such a mindset. We do not want a country which gives all the freedom to men, while women continue to live in a controlled environment. We will work together to end the patriarchal system in India,” Rahul said.In an Instagram story, Congress leader had also defended actor Kriti Sanon amid criticism of her outfit in a Raksha Bandhan advertisement, saying, “What a woman wears, what she does and where she goes — is her choice.”He added, “Stop trolling women for exercising their freedom,” using the hashtag “smash the patriarchy”.The remarks followed criticism of Sanon's attire in a jewellery advertisement, including from BJP MP Kangana Ranaut.Sanon subsequently questioned why women continued to be told what to wear and said, “Culture & Traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline!”
Article Summary: BJP leader and MP Bansuri Swaraj referred to Congress leader’s August 22 remarks at an event in Pune, where he spoke about challenging patriarchal attitudes and restrictions placed on women. “I want to ask Rahul Gandhi ji, do you limit the slogan of ‘smash the patriarchy’ only to the stage in Puni? Do you practise political patriarchy within your own Congress party?” she added.

Why did Victor Hedman leave Tampa Bay Lightning?

Why did Hedman believe stepping away helped Tampa Bay?

Victor Hedman’s decision to walk away from the Tampa Bay Lightning late in the 2025-26 season has received a clearer explanation during the NHL offseason. The veteran defenseman recently spoke publicly about the physical issues and performance anxiety that kept him out, including Tampa Bay’s first-round Stanley Cup Playoffs series versus the Montreal Canadiens. His remarks also brought up the issue of mental health in pro hockey.Victor Hedman is leaving the Tampa Bay Lightning, saying he needs to focus on his mental and physical health following a difficult stretch. The captain last played March 19, 2026, when he departed a 6-2 win over the Vancouver Canucks after one period. Six days later, Tampa Bay announced he was taking a leave of absence for personal reasons.“For me, it was not really feeling low, but it was performance anxiety, kind of feeling that pressure in your chest as soon as a game day would hit,” Hedman said. “It kind of locks you up. You make a mistake and in the past you’d be able to shake it off, but I couldn’t do that. And I wasn’t feeling 100 per cent physically.The news came after a season in which the 35-year-old defenseman was plagued by injuries. Hedman missed a lot of time with an elbow injury that required surgery, and then got hurt during warmups with Team Sweden before the 2026 Winter Olympics quarterfinal against the United States.He returned to Tampa Bay after the Olympic break, but he only played in 12 games before his last one of the season.Hedman ultimately felt the decision to step away was the right one for him and the TampaBay Lightning. He felt he was not playing like himself and not making the contribution expected of a long-time captain.The ruling forced Hedman to miss the final 15 games of the regular season and all seven games of Tampa Bay’s first-round playoff series against the Montreal Canadiens. The Lightning fell in Game 7 by a score of 2-1 on May 3. Hedman skated through the playoffs and mentioned he could have come back if Tampa Bay had advanced.Hedman, who is in his 18th NHL season with the Tampa Bay Lightning, said he feels better physically and mentally. He said it will take him a little while to get back into the rhythm of the game after not playing since March. But he has called himself motivated and confident for the upcoming season.His openness is a huge mental-health message to the N.H.L., too. Hedman has talked about the support he’s had from his therapist, teammates, family and others in the league. He hopes sharing his experience publicly will inspire others who are struggling to seek help, instead of going it alone.
Article Summary: Victor Hedman is leaving the Tampa Bay Lightning, saying he needs to focus on his mental and physical health following a difficult stretch. The captain last played March 19, 2026, when he departed a 6-2 win over the Vancouver Canucks after one period. Hedman ultimately felt the decision to step away was the right one for him and the TampaBay Lightning.

Article Title: Are Elliotte Friedman and Kevin Bieksa leaving Sportsnet as Amazon Prime Video expands NHL coverage in Canada
Article Text:
Canadian former ice hockey player Kevin Bieksa (L) and journalist Elliotte Friedman (R) are seen during training on day three of the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic games at Milano Santagiulia Ice Hockey Arena on February 09, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images)

Could Elliotte Friedman and Kevin Bieksa leave Sportsnet?

What could Amazon Prime Video offer Elliotte Friedman and Kevin Bieksa?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The futures of Elliotte Friedman and Kevin Bieksa in the broadcast booth are unclear, as neither has signed contracts with Sportsnet for the 2026-27 NHL season. Amazon Prime Video has emerged as a possible landing spot as it looks to build on its Canadian NHL coverage, but nothing has been finalised. Amazon will air a 12-year deal featuring Wednesday Nite Hockey in Canada and select playoff series. If either broadcaster comes on board, the move could reshape Sportsnet’s NHL presentation and give Amazon two established hockey voices as it builds out its coverage.Both exits are not confirmed, but Sportsnet could be without Friedman and Bieksa if contract talks don’t lead to new deals.The Toronto Star reported that Sportsnet had yet to sign contracts with the two broadcasters for next season. Amazon Prime Video was also highlighted as a possibility for both.At this point, the information available points toward uncertainty, not a concluded move. If the network strikes new deals with them, discussions can continue, and both analysts could stay with Sportsnet.Friedman is one of the most recognised NHL insiders in North American hockey media. He's become a go-to guy for trade rumours, free agency news and other league news through his reporting, including his work on 32 Thoughts.Bieksa has a different perspective. The former Vancouver Canucks defenceman moved into broadcasting after retirement and quickly developed a reputation as a loudmouth analyst with a unique personality.Their different styles make them a good television team. Friedman is mostly reporting and league information, while Bieksa provides former-player insight and a more direct analytical approach.Amazon’s growing presence in the NHL could be a good opportunity for both broadcasters.In its long-term deal, Amazon will televise Wednesday Nite Hockey and some playoff series in Canada beginning with the 2026-27 season. The deal gives the streaming service an increasingly important role in Canadian NHL broadcasts.Friedman and Bieksa could help Amazon gain instant credibility. Friedman would bring insider reporting and league-wide recognition, while Bieksa could provide analysis, personality and familiarity to viewers making the transition to the platform.If Sportsnet lost either of those broadcasters, its NHL panel would look different. If it lost both, its on-air persona could be radically changed.Sportsnet still has some seasoned personalities, including Ron MacLean, who is reportedly returning for the 2026-27 season. Friedman and Bieksa, however, play unique roles that cannot be easily duplicated.Neither Friedman nor Bieksa have publicly announced a final deal with Amazon Prime Video, and their Sportsnet futures are up in the air.So this is more of a developing story in broadcasting than a confirmed departure. There’s also the possibility that before the season begins, the contract talks could go a different way and both analysts end up remaining with Sportsnet.The big question right now is whether Sportsnet re-signs Friedman and Bieksa, or whether Amazon uses its growing NHL presence to add two of Canada’s best-known hockey broadcasters.
Article Summary: The futures of Elliotte Friedman and Kevin Bieksa are unclear. Neither has signed contracts with Sportsnet for the 2026-27 NHL season. Amazon Prime Video has emerged as a possible landing spot as it looks to build on its Canadian NHL coverage. Amazon will air a 12-year deal featuring Wednesday Nite Hockey and select playoff series.

Article Title: Pakistan-born ODI cricketer handed 15-month ban by ICC; here's why
Article Text:
United Arab Emirates (UAE) batter Asif Khan (Photo/ICC)

UAE batter Asif Khan has been banned for 15 months after testing positive for a banned anabolic steroid during an out-of-competition doping test conducted last year.Asif tested positive for a metabolite of mesterolone in a sample collected on September 8, 2025. Mesterolone is an anabolic steroid used to increase testosterone levels.The 36-year-old admitted to violating Article 2.1 of the ICC Anti-Doping Code and accepted the sanction through a Case Resolution Agreement with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and the International Cricket Council (ICC)."The 36-year-old admitted to a violation of Article 2.1 of the ICC Anti-Doping Code and accepted the sanction through a Case Resolution Agreement with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and the International Cricket Council (ICC)," read a statement from cricket's world governing body.The ban has been backdated to September 8, 2025 and will run until December 7, 2026. Asif will be allowed to resume training with a team or use the facilities of a club or other ICC Member organisation from October 8, but he will only be eligible to return to competitive cricket from December 8."Asif will be permitted to return to training with a team or use the facilities of a club or other ICC Member organisation from October 8, but will only be eligible to return to competitive cricket from December 8," the ICC statement said.The ICC has also disqualified Asif's individual results from September 8, 2025 until the start of his provisional suspension on December 29, 2025."This includes all resulting consequences, such as the loss of any medals, points, prize money or prizes."Asif, who was born in Pakistan and moved to the UAE in 2017, has represented the UAE in 38 ODIs and 56 T20 Internationals since making his international debut in 2022.Before moving to the UAE, the right-handed batter played 32 first-class matches in Pakistan's domestic cricket.
Article Summary: UAE batter Asif Khan has been banned for 15 months. Khan tested positive for a metabolite of mesterolone in a sample collected on September 8, 2025. The 36-year-old admitted to violating Article 2.1 of the ICC Anti-Doping Code.

Article Title: Why is Alex Nylander joining Calgary Flames after finding limited NHL opportunities with Toronto Maple Leafs

Why did Alex Nylander join Calgary Flames now?

After two seasons with the Toronto Maple Leafs organization, Alex Nylander is heading to the Calgary Flames on a professional tryout at training camp. The move gives the 28-year-old forward another shot at fighting for an NHL roster spot after limited action at the highest level in Toronto.This follows Nylander having one of his better recent seasons in the AHL with the Toronto Marlies. He played a part in helping the Marlies to a Calder Cup win, but his NHL opportunities remained scarce.The pro tryout provides Alex Nylander another chance to vie for NHL employment, and it also means he’s in the Calgary Flames’ training-camp plans.Nylander had 24 goals, 29 assists and 53 points in 65 regular-season games with the Toronto Marlies in the 2025-26 AHL season. Article Title: Travis Kelce’s alleged $12.9M donation to help homeless families exposed as a completely fabricated story

A viral story portraying Travis Kelce as a major force in the fight against homelessness has once again made its way across social media. The claim sounds inspiring, but it is not true. Snopes has rated the story false, finding no credible evidence that the Kansas City Chiefs star donated $12.9 million in bonuses and endorsements to build homes for people experiencing homelessness.The Facebook posts claimed Kelce had donated his “entire” $12.9 million in bonuses and endorsements to an organization called the Homeless Housing Initiative. According to the posts, the money would fund 150 homes containing 300 beds.The story also included an emotional statement supposedly delivered by Kelce at a press conference:“I witnessed the impact of homelessness firsthand as a child, and I knew that if I ever had the means, I would make a meaningful contribution,” Travis Kelce said at a press conference. “No one deserves to sleep on the streets.”There was one major problem. No credible record of Kelce making those remarks could be found.Snopes reported that searches for the supposed quote produced no reliable news coverage. That matters because a public announcement involving millions of dollars and a major construction project would normally attract substantial attention from sports and mainstream news outlets.The alleged charity also raised another red flag. Snopes found no listing for the Homeless Housing Initiative in Charity Navigator, adding to the evidence that the organization described in the viral posts was not legitimate.The posts gained considerable traction, with several identical versions collecting tens of thousands of reactions. Their popularity, however, did not make the claim any more credible.The false donation story is particularly convincing because Kelce has an established record of charitable work. He has used his platform to support causes through his Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation, making it easy for a fabricated story to appear believable.Kelce himself addressed a similar false story on the April 9, 2025, episode of his “New Heights” podcast. While discussing the real work of his foundation, he pushed back against fabricated reports circulating online.“This time I wasn't doing what was falsely claimed by the social channels or the outlets posting all this AI stuff,” Kelce said.The financial details in the latest rumor also do not fit Kelce's known earnings. Forbes reported that Kelce was making about $30 million from endorsements in 2025. He and his brother, Jason Kelce, also signed a three-year, $100 million deal with Wondery for their “New Heights” podcast in 2024.That does not prove that Kelce would never make a donation of this size. It does show why the specific $12.9 million figure deserves scrutiny.There are genuine examples of NFL players helping people facing homelessness. Former NFL player Jordan Jenkins bought two duplexes and donated them to The Plummer Home to help house homeless veterans. Warrick Dunn has also spent years providing homes to families through his charitable foundation.Those real efforts highlight the key lesson behind the Kelce rumor. A heartwarming story can spread quickly, but generosity should be verified rather than assumed. In this case, the viral claim about Travis Kelce donating $12.9 million and funding 150 homes was simply not supported by the evidence.
Article Summary: A viral story portraying Travis Kelce as a major force in the fight against homelessness has once again made its way across social media. No credible record of Kelce making those remarks could be found. A heartwarming story can spread quickly, but generosity should be verified rather than assumed.

The Indian women’s hockey team will look to end their World Cup campaign on a high when they face Germany in the fifth-sixth place classification match at Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen on Thursday.Having played five matches so far, India have won one, drawn three and lost only once — against hosts Netherlands. It has been an impressive campaign for a team that looked out of sorts last year, and coach Sjoerd Marijne has been more than pleased with the progress his wards have made.“I told the girls, ‘If I had told you six months ago that we would play a quarterfinal against Australia at the World Cup and draw 0-0, would you have believed it?’ I don’t think, considering the position they were in six months ago, they would have believed it,” said Marijne in a video released by Hockey India.Indeed, India have produced a fascinating campaign, with almost everyone contributing at different stages. The only glaring gap has been their inability to convert chances into goals consistently — something that eventually ended their hopes of reaching the semifinals.“We have really made good progress, and it’s not easy to score goals against these teams. The basis of our game is our defence, and we do that really well,” Marijne said.Apart from their games against China and South Africa, India failed to score against England, Netherlands and Australia. It was not for a lack of opportunities, but rather their inability to make those chances count when it mattered most.That will once again be put to the test against Germany, coached by a familiar face in former India head coach Janneke Schopman.Germany, too, have been through a transition since the Paris Olympics and could not make the semifinals after losing their two crucial matches against Argentina and Belgium. They did, however, win three matches across the two rounds, while scoring 13 goals in the process.Their ability to find the net has been one of their biggest positives, but breaking down India’s defence could prove a different challenge.Schopman knows this Indian team well from her time as their head coach and is likely to have plenty of insight into how to exploit their weaknesses. However, India have shown they can be extremely difficult to break down when they get their defensive structure right.England had 20 shots on goal and 12 penalty corners in their 0-0 draw with India, while Australia managed 13 shots and five penalty corners in India's last game. Neither could find a way past the Indian defence.Speaking about the Australia match, Marijne said, “We evaluated the game with the team, and sometimes these things happen in a process. Sometimes you take a step back to make two steps forward. Anaya Bangar's return to competitive cricket now has a potential timeline, with March 2027 set as the key date in her bid to pursue elite women's cricket in Australia and potentially earn a route into the Women's Big Bash League.The former Mumbai U-19 cricketer has been cleared by Cricket Australia to play community cricket and has been given a pathway to pursue elite women's cricket, subject to the governing body's eligibility requirements.Bangar, the daughter of former India cricketer and ex-India batting coach Sanjay Bangar , stressed that the clearance does not amount to selection for the WBBL or automatic entry into elite cricket. Instead, it gives her an opportunity to work towards that level.“I am preparing to return to women’s cricket in Australia with the aim of pursuing elite cricket from March 2027,” the 25-year-old said. “This has not been an automatic or an informal process. Cricket Australia has a framework designed to balance fairness, competitive integrity, and inclusion in women’s sport, and my case has been considered through that framework.”Bangar said she understands that she will have to earn any opportunity that comes her way.“Cricket Australia has given me a pathway, which does not mean that I have been given a place in a team. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,” she said.Bangar's immediate plan is to find a club and play community cricket in Australia as she works towards a return to the competitive game. Her participation in elite competitions, including the WBBL, will depend on Cricket Australia's Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy.Under the policy, a player's serum testosterone concentration must remain below 10 nmol/L for at least 12 months to qualify for elite cricket.Bangar's eligibility will be assessed from March 2027, including through a required blood test.“My understanding from Cricket Australia's clearance is that my eligibility for elite women's cricket from March 2027 remains subject to the applicable policy requirements, including a blood test assessment at the same time. If that March 2027 test confirms that I continue to meet the required testosterone criteria, I will be eligible to pursue selection for elite women’s cricket, including the Women’s Big Bash League pathway,” Bangar said.Meeting those requirements would allow Bangar to seek selection, but would not guarantee her a place in an elite team.“I don’t expect my history or my identity to earn me a place on a cricket team. I want my cricket to earn me a place on a cricket team,” she said.Bangar had earlier sought clarity from the Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ) over whether transgender athletes could compete in women's cricket in India. She said she received no response to a letter submitted last year.She subsequently approached Cricket Australia in June this year.According to Bangar, Cricket Australia assessed her medical records, blood tests, documents relating to her surgeries and a research report from Manchester Metropolitan University's Institute of Sport before reaching its decision.“After I published my athlete testing report and everything else, BCCI stayed quiet about it. Whereas Cricket Australia actually read my report, went through all my medical history and had a proper team assessing my case,” Bangar said.“I approached Cricket Australia and they gave me clearance to play in terms of fairness and inclusivity.”Bangar is now looking for a club in Australia, with community cricket set to be the first step in her attempt to rebuild her playing career and eventually pursue an opportunity in elite women's cricket.
Article Summary: Anaya Bangar has been cleared by Cricket Australia to play community cricket and has been given a pathway to pursue elite women's cricket. The 25-year-old's eligibility will be assessed from March 2027, including through a required blood test. Her participation in elite competitions, including the WBBL, will depend on Cricket Australia's Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy.

Kyle Singler, 38, wanders from room to room, appears to be agitated, describing a life that sounds nothing like the one he built during his NBA years. He says his power has been shut off. He says his house has been broken into. He says money is being drained from accounts he can barely track anymore.None of that has been independently verified. But the pattern is familiar to anyone who followed his last public flare-up. Back in November 2024, Singler posted something similar, telling followers he feared for his life every single day. This week's videos pick up roughly where that one left off, only louder and more disjointed.There's also history sitting underneath all of this. Singler was arrested in Oklahoma last October after his girlfriend told police he grabbed her by the head and shoved her to the ground during an argument at an Airbnb, with their child present. He posted bond on a misdemeanor charge and the case has largely stayed out of headlines since, until now.Singler didn't just vent about strangers or unnamed enemies. He went after Krzyzewski directly, the coach who guided him to a national title in 2010 and later called him one of the most complete players he'd ever developed.Singler claims he reached out for help and got nothing back. "Coach K has set me up, man," he said in one clip, adding that Krzyzewski had "fully dismissed" his messages.“You guys are cutting my power off, breaking into my house, stealing money, ruining my life. I reached out to Coach K and all he did was sit me on the bench. Thanks, man. Is that what we're doing at that school, sitting people down, teaching them up? Cool beans, man.Coach, where you at? Help a brother out. Thought we were on the same team, man," Singler shared.He described feeling abandoned by the program he once helped define, at one point comparing his situation to being benched, as though the man who shaped his career had simply stopped answering the phone.It's worth remembering where Singler came from. He was the engine of Duke's 2010 championship run, earned Most Outstanding Player honors in that tournament, and went on to play seven NBA seasons split between Detroit and Oklahoma City after going 33rd overall in 2011. He pulled in more than $22 million over his career, most of it from a contract extension with the Thunder.
Article Summary: Former Duke star Kyle Singler posted a string of rambling Instagram videos this week. The clips show him pacing through what looks like an empty house, insisting people are trying to hurt him and take his money. Singler was arrested in Oklahoma last October after his girlfriend told police he grabbed her by the head.

Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard has become the highest run-scorer in T20 cricket after going past England batter Jos Buttler 's tally during the Caribbean Premier League (CPL) 2026.Pollard entered the record books on Thursday when he scored 65 off 26 balls for Trinbago Knight Riders against Saint Lucia Kings at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba.The former Mumbai Indians player needed 35 runs before the match to move past Buttler, who had 14,890 T20 runs.Earlier this year, Pollard had overtaken Chris Gayle to become the highest run-scorer in T20 cricket. Buttler then moved ahead of him in August 2026 while playing for Manchester Super Giants in The Hundred. Pollard has now reclaimed the top spot.The 39-year-old now has 14,921 runs from 666 innings in 749 T20 matches.Pollard will get a chance to become the first player to score 15,000 runs in T20 cricket when Trinbago Knight Riders face Barbados Tridents at the same venue on Friday (Saturday IST).His innings came at a strike rate of 250 and included six fours and five sixes while chasing a target of 212 for the Andre Russell-led Trinbago Knight Riders.The five sixes also took Pollard's career tally to 1,010 sixes in T20 cricket. He is now 47 sixes away from Chris Gayle's record for the most sixes in the format.Pollard and Gayle are the only players to hit more than 1,000 sixes in T20 cricket. Andre Russell is third on the list with 808 sixes.

Article Title: After 75 years the Pro Bowl is dead: Here's what replaces the game nobody wanted to watch
Article Text:
NFL ends the Pro Bowl game after 75 years (Via X)

Why did the NFL cancel the Pro Bowl game?

What happens to the Pro Bowl now that the game is gone?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NFL officially ended the Pro Bowl game on Wednesday, closing out a 75-year tradition that had slowly lost the plot. The league announced at its owners meeting in Atlanta that no game will be played after this season. Players selected as Pro Bowlers will still receive the honor and gather in Los Angeles for a celebration, but the actual football game is gone. This is not a pause. The NFL is not regrouping. It is a full stop on what had become the most skippable event on the sports calendar.The honest answer is that the players stopped caring, and the league finally admitted it out loud. NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent spoke directly with more than a dozen star players this summer, and what he heard was consistent. They did not want competitive football after the playoffs ended. Vincent put it plainly at the owners meeting: "You come off the championship games and the viewers see the physicality of the game and you try to replicate that. Frankly, it just doesn't sit well. This isn't a good representation."That admission matters more than it might seem. For years the NFL kept pushing the format, hoping a tweak would fix the problem.The game moved out of Honolulu, the home it had for decades. In 2023 the league switched entirely to flag football, hoping the casual format would generate energy. It did not. Ratings stayed soft. Players showed up out of obligation, not excitement. Nobody was fooled.Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president overseeing events, framed the decision with uncommon directness. "It's OK to be the first league to walk away from a competitive all-star game," he said in Atlanta. That line will not make headlines for its poetry, but it signals something real: the NFL is no longer interested in defending a product it cannot fix.The title survives. The game does not. The NFL confirmed that 88 players will still earn Pro Bowl recognition after this season and be honored at an event in Los Angeles. Several flag football exhibitions will take place around that time, though they will serve as entertainment rather than competition. The core distinction, being named one of the best at your position in the NFL, stays intact.The league also eliminated replacement selections going forward. In the past, injured players or Super Bowl participants were swapped out for alternates, which diluted the honor. Cleveland Browns rookie quarterback Shedeur Sanders made the Pro Bowl this year as a replacement. Under the new structure, that category is gone. If a player earns it, they earn it outright.O'Reilly explained the thinking behind the restructured honor: "The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL. A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans."The voting process stays the same: an equal split between players, coaches, and fans. What changes is the weight behind it. Without a game to water things down, a Pro Bowl selection becomes a cleaner acknowledgment of a great season rather than a footnote to an event most people forgot was happening.
Article Summary: The Pro Bowl game will not be played after this season, the NFL announced Wednesday. The league says the players did not want competitive football after the playoffs ended. The game moved out of Honolulu, the home it had for decades, and the league switched to flag football.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I almost died after giving birth to my daughter.” - How Serena Williams turned life-threatening motherhood and family strength into sporting resilience
Article Text:
Serena Williams makes Cincinnati return with Venus after ‘emotional’ family moment with daughters Olympia and Adira

How did Serena Williams almost die after giving birth to Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr.

How did Alexis Ohanian support Serena Williams during her recovery

How did Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. become Serena Williams’ motivation

Why did Serena Williams choose family when she stepped away from tennis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Serena Williams’ story of motherhood is also a story of survival. In 2017, the tennis star won the Australian Open while eight weeks pregnant, then nearly died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals. Her daughter Olympia became an important part of that journey. Years later, Serena chose to step away from singles tennis to focus on her family, while continuing to build her life beyond the court.Serena’s pregnancy had gone well, but the birth of Olympia on September 1, 2017, quickly became dangerous. Olympia was delivered by emergency C-section after her heart rate dropped sharply during contractions. The surgery itself went well, and Serena was able to hold her daughter. The serious problems started about a day later.Serena suddenly had trouble breathing. Because she had a history of blood clots, she suspected she was having another pulmonary embolism, a condition in which a blood clot blocks blood flow in the lungs.She asked for a CT scan and blood thinner treatment. Doctors later found several small clots in her lungs.The treatment then caused another problem. Serena’s intense coughing made her C-section wound open. Doctors found a large hematoma, or a collection of blood, in her abdomen. She needed more surgery and another procedure to help stop future clots from reaching her lungs. After leaving the hospital, Serena spent the first six weeks of motherhood in bed and had difficulty even walking.Serena later described the experience in a CNN opinion piece, making clear just how close she believed she had come to losing her life.“I almost died after giving birth to my daughter, Olympia. Yet I consider myself fortunate… When I finally made it home to my family, with only days left in my recovery, I felt a deep sense of gratitude just to hold my baby girl in my arms.”The CNN piece was also about the wider problem of maternal health and the need for better access to care. Serena credited the doctors and nurses who treated her with helping save her life.For Serena, recovering from childbirth was not only about getting her body strong enough to play tennis again. She was also learning how to care for a newborn while she was unable to move normally.Her husband, Alexis Ohanian, was there during that difficult period. In Serena’s 2018 Vogue interview, Ohanian spoke about how hard it was to watch his wife struggle while he could not take away what she was going through. Serena also described how difficult those first weeks were as a new mother.That made her return to tennis different from any comeback she had made before. She was not simply trying to get her ranking back. She was trying to find a way to be a professional athlete and a mother at the same time.When Serena returned to competition, she faced another challenge. After her long break, she had fallen far down the rankings and had to work her way back into major events. She eventually reached the 2018 Wimbledon final, less than a year after giving birth.Olympia was born into a world where her mother was already one of the biggest names in tennis. But after the difficult birth, motherhood gave Serena a different reason to keep going.During her return, Serena spoke openly about the emotional side of being a mother and an athlete. Her run to the Wimbledon final in 2018 became one of the clearest signs that she could still compete at the highest level after everything her body had gone through.After the Wimbledon final, Serena also dedicated her performance to mothers watching her. She had lost to Angelique Kerber, but the result did not take away from what she had achieved by reaching the final so soon after giving birth.“Olympia, does mama look good out here? You’re the reason I’m here, you’re my motivation. To all the moms out there, I was playing for you today. It’s okay to have hard days, but we keep fighting.”That message summed up what her comeback had come to mean. Serena was not hiding the difficult parts of motherhood. She was showing that returning to work after having a child can involve fear, setbacks and days when the body simply does not cooperate.Her run did not stop at Wimbledon. Serena reached four straight Grand Slam singles finals after becoming a mother: Wimbledon and the US Open in 2018, followed by the Australian Open and Wimbledon in 2019. She did not win those finals, but reaching them showed how quickly she had returned to the top of the sport.By 2022, Serena was ready for another major change. She did not want to call it retirement. In her Vogue essay announcing her decision to move away from professional tennis, she called it an “evolution.”Her decision was closely tied to her family. Serena wrote about Olympia’s wish to become a big sister and her own desire to have another child. At the same time, she wanted to give more attention to Serena Ventures and the other parts of her life that had grown alongside her tennis career.“I have never liked the word retirement… Maybe the best word to describe what I’m up to is evolution. I’m here to tell you that I’m evolving away from tennis, toward other things that are important to me… My daughter wants to be a big sister, and I want to be there for my family.”Vogue published Serena’s essay in August 2022, ahead of what she described as her final US Open. She later welcomed her second daughter, Adira River Ohanian, with Alexis Ohanian in August 2023.Serena’s tennis story has since taken another unexpected turn. In 2026, she returned to competitive tennis, making her comeback first in doubles and later joining Carlos Alcaraz for the US Open mixed doubles event. That means her relationship with the sport is still evolving, even after she stepped away from singles competition in 2022.Her motherhood journey remains one of the most personal parts of that story. Serena went from a frightening medical crisis after Olympia’s birth to competing in Grand Slam finals again. She then made a choice to put family at the centre of her next chapter. For Serena, strength was not only about winning another match. It was also about surviving, recovering and finding a new reason to keep moving forward.
Article Summary: Serena Williams almost died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals.

Article Title: "I’ve sacrificed a lot": Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' director Kelli Finglass confronts the possibility of walking away from the America's Sweetheart
Article Text:
America’s Sweethearts

Kelli Finglass on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and social media criticism

Kelli Finglass reveals her future with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Kelli Finglass , leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her at the center of auditions, tough decisions, television scrutiny and the changing pressures faced by young performers. As Netflix’sreturns for season three, Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away.Kelli Finglass knows exactly what it takes to become a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader because she once stood where the dancers now stand. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her career has since become closely tied to the evolution of the organization on television.The Netflix series has brought unprecedented attention to the cheerleaders, but that visibility has a downside. Social media criticism can follow the women beyond the dance studio, something Finglass says she has seen affect members of the team.She does not make a habit of reading online comments herself. Still, she understands the emotional weight they can carry.“The words of people, while they can be very, very uplifting...Like in my personal case with my skin cancer journey, the people that reached out to me were extremely supportive," she said in an interview with Vanity Fair."Words can hurt and they can also heal. I’m trusting humanity to help figure this one out because it’s a much bigger thing than I can solve. But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.”That outlook reflects a major lesson Finglass has learned through years of television. The cheerleaders do not need to appear perfect all the time.Kelli Finglass has also reconsidered what leadership means as she has grown older. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances.Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.“I spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what we’ve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive. People love when they can relate to somebody, and that’s been an unexpected “aha” for me—for these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles, has, I hope, given viewers something to find hope in and find something they can relate to.”..Now entering her 35th season with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, retirement is no longer an impossible thought. Finglass says her family could ultimately influence that decision, especially as she looks toward becoming a grandmother someday.“I have, but we’re so busy, we don’t have time to think about anything except the next hour. It would be a personal decision. I’ve sacrificed a lot of time with my family. My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandma…I want that time if and when I have grandchildren. That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.”For now, Finglass remains focused on the next generation. Her story has become intertwined with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, but her lasting message may be simpler: perfection is impressive, while vulnerability can be powerful.
Article Summary: Kelli Finglass performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances. Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.

India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel.The bowlers had only a short window to work with, but Krishna made it count, picking up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over.Krishna said aggression is not necessarily about showing emotion or getting into a verbal battle with the opposition.“Yeah, I would like to say so. I mean, aggression can come out in different ways, and for me it is about what I'm doing when I'm bowling. It's very easy for people to get away or be distracted by what's happening in the pitch.There's too much happening, there's not too much happening, but I think the focus is still to come in and bowl those areas with full effort,” Krishna told the broadcasters before the start of Day 3’s play.Krishna bowled back of a length outside off and found enough movement from the surface to trouble Lahiru Udara. The Sri Lankan opener edged towards gully, where Yashasvi Jaiswal completed an excellent diving catch to dismiss him for one.Krishna said the wicket was a result of both the conditions and Jaiswal’s fielding effort.“Yeah, I think it was, there’s something in the pitch, of course. Maybe stopped a little bit. There was a bit of seam, and I think credit goes to Jaiswal for the catch that he took. It was an exceptional one. We have been putting in some effort on the field in practice, so I think it just paid off,” he mentioned.India had very little time to bowl before bad light stopped play. Manav Suthar then dismissed Prabath Jayasuriya for two with the final delivery of the day, leaving Sri Lanka at 8/2.Krishna stressed that creating chances is only half the job and the fielders also need to complete the opportunity.“100%. I think 50% of the job is bowling the ball there, getting an edge, but 50% is taking it as well, and we have been pretty good at doing that. I think it's also doing the simple things right, which we have been doing well, and that's what shows,” he added.Krishna also spoke about the need to adjust his length according to the pitch. He said the Indian coaching and analysis staff work together to decide the right approach for each surface.“Length is something that keeps changing with pitches that we play on. So we sit with analysts, coaches, and everything and decide on what's the kind of length that we want to be bowling on different surfaces. And yeah, natural length was something that I could say when I was not playing for the country, but when I'm here I need to be bowling every length that the team wants, and I'm trying to do that,” he concluded.
Article Summary: India pacer Prasidh Krishna believes aggression is best shown through his bowling. Krishna picked up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over. India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel. Sri Lanka were reduced to 8/2 before bad light ended Day Two.

Article Title: Kangana Ranaut slams Kriti Sanon ad, asks ‘why would you tie rakhi in bikini?’

Kangana Ranaut stirred controversy by critiquing Kriti Sanon's outfit featured in a Raksha Bandhan advertisement

Kangana Ranaut instagram story

Our closets are full of variety of clothes, today's woman is a global woman. Article Title: 'Haven't achieved 1% of my success': Kangana Ranaut slams critics, targets Baba Ramdev over comments on women
Article Text:
Kangana Ranaut criticized film industry figures and Baba Ramdev for their remarks





NEW DELHI: BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut on Monday hit back at several film industry figures and yoga guru Baba Ramdev over their criticism of her recent remarks, accusing her detractors of targeting her for publicity.Speaking to reporters at Delhi Airport, Ranaut said she would not take advice from people who, according to her, had not achieved comparable professional success.“Every day, I see people like Ashutosh Rana — who says I bark like a dog — or the likes of Sonu Sood. Then there are people like Rakhi Sawant, who make all sorts of remarks about my character, and Taapsee Pannu, who insults my parents, my upbringing and my background,” she said.Ranaut described her critics as “failed” and “completely irrelevant” people who, she alleged, abuse her to gain media attention.“If you haven't achieved even one per cent of the success I have in life, I am not going to listen to you,” she said, adding that she would not tolerate what she called personal attacks.Ranaut also hit out at Baba Ramdev over his remarks on women, saying he had “crossed every boundary of decency”.“The kind of comments he has made about a woman have shamed society. Given the remarks he makes about women, I think he really needs to reflect on his perspective regarding them,” she said.The latest exchange follows the controversy over Ranaut's “Generation Gutter” remark while criticising protesters at Jantar Mantar. Her comments triggered criticism from several public figures, including Sonu Sood and Rakhi Sawant.The controversy also brought her longstanding differences with actors Taapsee Pannu and Ashutosh Rana into focus. Ramdev had separately criticised Ranaut's remarks about the younger generation, leading to a public exchange between the two.Ranaut, who represents Himachal Pradesh's Mandi Lok Sabha constituency, has frequently been involved in public disagreements with personalities from the film industry and other public figures.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: Kangana Ranaut says she will not take advice from people who have not achieved comparable professional success. She also hit out at Baba Ramdev over his remarks on women, saying he had “crossed every boundary of decency’ The latest exchange follows the controversy over her ‘Generation Gutter’ remark.

Article Title: Kylie Kelce gets emotional recalling the miscarriage that made her terrified to try again
Article Text:
Kylie Kelce

Kylie Kelce admits the fear of trying again after her miscarriage never really went away

Why she keeps returning to this story

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby after her 2018 miscarriage, the mom of four didn't hedge, she confirmed the fear was real, and it stuck around a lot longer than most people would expect.Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month, explaining that a doctor's visit before the birth of her eldest daughter, Wyatt, confirmed there was no heartbeat.The timing made it worse, the diagnosis fell on her husband Jason's birthday, and she initially couldn't bring herself to break the news to him that day. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again.According to Kelce, getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it. In early pregnancy, she found herself checking survival odds on a near-weekly basis, and by the later stages of her second trimester, that worry shifted into wondering whether a baby born that day could make it. She's been candid that this obsessive tracking wasn't necessarily a healthy habit, just one that helped her get through it, and one that carried into her later pregnancies too.Kelce didn't have to revisit this topic; she's already raising four young daughters, and the loss happened years ago.But her reasoning for continuing to talk about it is straightforward. She views grief from pregnancy loss as something with no real end date, capable of resurfacing unexpectedly no matter how much time has passed or how many kids follow.It's a theme she's returned to more than once, and each time she's shared it, she's said the response from others tends to be more stories of loss rather than awkward silence.She was careful not to frame the fear as the end of the story, either. Her bottom line was that avoiding the risk entirely would have meant never having Wyatt at all, so for her, moving forward despite the fear was worth it. It's a message that fits her reputation for being unusually direct about hard topics, and one she's now delivered twice, in two different ways, likely for the benefit of anyone quietly sitting with the same fear.
Article Summary: Kylie Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again. Getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it.

Bringing motorsport to the community
